description:
Workspace-wide pattern: every extension-server MemoryBackend has many `std::sync::Mutex::lock().unwrap()` sites without a documented panic policy. Workspace AGENTS.md says 'No `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` in library code — propagate errors with ?', but Mutex::lock returning PoisonError only on prior-thread-panic-with-guard-held is the canonical implicit exception in std-library Rust. The current bare `.unwrap()` at every call site is what downstream contributors will copy from these 'reference implementations' without thinking about the policy.

Site counts (cargo grep, 2026-05-15):
- jmap-mail-server (CANONICAL): 31 sites of .lock().unwrap() in src/memory.rs; 3 sparse 'test only: mutex is never poisoned in tests' comments at lines 2438/2543/2682; no module-level policy.
- jmap-metadata-server: ~23 sites across src/memory.rs and src/lib.rs (per bd:JMAP-826m.48); no policy comment.
- Other 6 extension-server siblings (chat/calendars/tasks/contacts/filenode/sharing): unaudited, expected similar.

Approach options:
(a) Add a single module-level rustdoc paragraph in mail-server's src/memory.rs explaining the policy ('Mutex::lock unwrap is intentional: poisoning indicates a prior-thread panic-with-guard-held, which is a programmer bug under #[forbid(unsafe_code)]. Tests in this crate never trigger it; a production backend that wants graceful poison handling should re-implement the trait with non-bare-unwrap locking.'). Propagate the same paragraph to all 7 siblings.
(b) Introduce a private `fn lock_state(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Inner>` helper in each MemoryBackend; document the policy once at the helper; replace all bare .lock().unwrap() sites with the helper. Same propagation across 7 siblings.
(c) Convert all bare .unwrap() to .expect('Mutex poisoned — prior thread panicked with guard held') with a stable greppable string. Per-site cost but per-panic discoverability.

Recommendation: (a). Cheapest, signals policy without churn, leaves the call sites readable. (b) reads cleaner but a sweep of 31+23+6×~20 ≈ 180 sites for a no-behavior-change refactor is harder to justify than the module-level paragraph. (c) is fine in principle but verbose.

Per the workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template propagation rule, this MUST start at jmap-mail-server and propagate to all 7 extension-server siblings in the same pass (or a follow-up sweep bead before merging).

Discovered while triaging bd:JMAP-826m.48; closing that sibling-scoped bead in favor of this workspace-scoped one.
title: Workspace-canonical-first: document Mutex lock-unwrap panic policy in MemoryBackend (jmap-mail-server canonical, propagate to 7 siblings)
